sections.title: THERE IS A MRGL RISK OF SVR TSTMS OVER PORTIONS OF NC/SC/GA
sections.text: ...SUMMARY... SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS CAPABLE OF ISOLATED LARGE HAIL...WIND DAMAGE AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES ARE EXPECTED ACROSS MUCH OF MINNESOTA AND WESTERN WISCONSIN AND INTO PARTS OF THE MID-MISSOURI VALLEY AREA ON SATURDAY...WITH MARGINALLY SEVERE STORMS EXTENDING SOUTHWEST ACROSS KANSAS INTO NORTHEAST NEW MEXICO. A FEW STRONG/ISOLATED SEVERE STORMS ARE ALSO EXPECTED OVER PARTS OF THE SOUTHEAST.

sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: AS A MID-LEVEL TROUGH CONTINUES MOVING EWD ACROSS THE WRN ATLANTIC/AWAY FROM THE ERN SEABOARD...THE MAIN FEATURE ALOFT WITH RESPECT TO CONVECTIVE WEATHER WILL BE A LOW MOVING ENEWD ACROSS THE NRN PLAINS AND ADJACENT PARTS OF SASKATCHEWAN AND MANITOBA THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AND EVENING HOURS. OTHERWISE...LARGE-SCALE RIDGING IS PROGGED TO PREVAIL OVER THE SRN HALF OF THE COUNTRY. AT THE SURFACE...A COLD FRONTAL SURGE IS FORECAST ACROSS MN/IA DURING THE AFTERNOON...AND ACROSS WI AND WRN UPPER MI THROUGH THE SECOND HALF OF THE PERIOD. MEANWHILE...THE TRAILING PORTION OF THE BOUNDARY FARTHER TO THE SW WILL SHIFT MORE SLOWLY EWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS. FINALLY...A WEAK/REMNANT COLD FRONT OVER THE SOUTHEAST U.S. IS FORECAST TO SAG GRADUALLY SWD ACROSS THE SOUTHEAST WITH TIME...WITH A WEAK FRONTAL WAVE EXPECTED TO LINGER OVER THE GA/SC AREA THROUGH THE AFTERNOON AND EVENING HOURS.

sections.title: UPPER MS VALLEY AREA SWWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: THUNDERSTORMS -- MAINLY N OF THE INTERNATIONAL BORDER -- SHOULD BE ONGOING AT THE START OF THE PERIOD...WITH SOME POTENTIAL THAT THE SRN FRINGE OF THESE STORMS AND SOME ASSOCIATED SEVERE THREAT MAY BRUSH PARTS OF THE NRN MN VICINITY DURING THE MORNING. MEANWHILE...STEADILY FALLING MID-LEVEL HEIGHTS ACROSS MN THROUGH THE DAY AHEAD OF THE ADVANCING UPPER LOW AND THE APPROACH OF THE ASSOCIATED SURFACE COLD FRONT WILL SUPPORT AFTERNOON THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT IN A N-S ZONE ALONG THE BOUNDARY...AS MODERATE AIRMASS DESTABILIZATION OCCURS. WHILE LIKELY DEVELOPING IN A NNE-SSW BAND...STORMS MAY REMAIN CELLULAR INITIALLY...WITH INCREASINGLY STRONG/VEERING FLOW WITH HEIGHT SUPPORTING SUPERCELL STORM MODE AND ASSOCIATED POTENTIAL FOR VERY LARGE HAIL...STRONG/DAMAGING WINDS...AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES. WITH TIME...STORMS CROSSING MN AND -- DURING THE EVENING -- SHIFTING INTO WI SHOULD BECOME MORE LINEAR IN ORGANIZATION...WITH DAMAGING WINDS TO POSSIBLY BECOME THE PREDOMINANT SEVERE RISK. FARTHER TO THE SW...STORMS SHOULD REMAIN MORE ISOLATED FROM IA SWWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS ALONG THE FRONT. WHILE AMPLE CAPE WILL SUPPORT VIGOROUS UPDRAFTS...FLOW ALOFT WILL WEAKEN SUBSTANTIALLY WITH SWWD

sections.title: PORTIONS OF THE CAROLINAS INTO SRN GA
sections.text: DIURNAL HEATING OF A MOIST BOUNDARY LAYER OVER THE AREA WILL RESULT IN MODERATE DESTABILIZATION...WHICH WILL FUEL DEVELOPMENT OF ISOLATED TO SCATTERED STORMS -- PRIMARILY INVOF THE COLD FRONT SAGGING GRADUALLY SWD ACROSS THE AREA...AND AN ASSOCIATED/WEAK FRONTAL WAVE PROGGED INVOF THE SC/GA VICINITY DURING THE AFTERNOON. WHILE LOW-LEVEL FLOW SHOULD REMAIN WEAK...REMNANT/MODEST NWLY MID- TO UPPER-LEVEL FLOW MAY SUPPORT A FEW LOOSELY ORGANIZED STORMS/CLUSTERS OF STORMS...CAPABLE OF GUSTY WINDS AND POSSIBLY MARGINAL HAIL AS THEY SHIFT SWD/SEWD INTO EARLY EVENING. ..GOSS/COOK.. 06/25/2016

outlooks.summary: SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS...AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES ARE EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON INTO EARLY TONIGHT ACROSS MUCH OF MINNESOTA AND WESTERN WISCONSIN. A MORE MARGINAL SEVERE STORM RISK WILL EXTEND SOUTHWESTWARD INTO THE CENTRAL PLAINS. ISOLATED STRONG STORMS ARE ALSO EXPECTED OVER PARTS OF THE SOUTHEAST.

sections.title: UPPER MS VALLEY THROUGH TONIGHT
sections.text: A PRONOUNCED MIDLEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH OVER MT WILL PROGRESS EWD TO ND/MN...AS AN ASSOCIATED SURFACE CYCLONE DEVELOPS NWD FROM SE ND TO SRN MB AND OCCLUDES BY TONIGHT. S OF THE SURFACE CYCLONE...A COLD FRONT WILL CONTINUE TO MOVE EWD FROM THE ERN DAKOTAS INTO MN THIS AFTERNOON AND WI TONIGHT. THE COLD FRONT WILL PROVIDE THE PRIMARY FOCUS FOR SEVERE THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT THIS AFTERNOON INTO EARLY TONIGHT ACROSS THE UPPER MS VALLEY. BOUNDARY LAYER DEWPOINTS NEAR 70 F HAVE SPREAD NWD FROM MO/IA INTO CENTRAL MN...BENEATH A PLUME OF STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES. FARTHER N...SLIGHTLY ELEVATED STORMS ARE ONGOING OVER N/NE MN IN A LOW-LEVEL WAA REGIME...AND THESE STORMS WILL POSE AN ISOLATED HAIL RISK THROUGH THE FIRST PART OF THE DAY. ADDITIONAL THUNDERSTORM DEVELOPMENT WILL OCCUR BY MID AFTERNOON ACROSS CENTRAL MN AS THE LEADING EDGE OF THE MIDLEVEL HEIGHT FALLS/ASCENT COINCIDE WITH THE BAND OF LOW-LEVEL ASCENT ALONG THE COLD FRONT NEAR PEAK HEATING. FORECAST SOUNDINGS HAVE BEEN CONSISTENT IN SHOWING STRONG BUOYANCY /MLCAPE OF 3000-4000 J PER KG/...BUT SOME WEAKNESS IN THE MIDLEVEL FLOW WITHIN THE PRE-FRONTAL WARM SECTOR AS THE STRONGER MIDLEVEL FLOW LAGS TO THE W. LINEAR FORCING FOR AS

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS/MID MO VALLEY AREA THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: A SURFACE COLD FRONT WILL MOVE SEWD ACROSS NW IA/NEB/NW KS/ERN CO BY THIS EVENING. THE STRONGER FLOW AND DEEP-LAYER VERTICAL SHEAR WILL REMAIN N OF THIS CORRIDOR...AND THERE WILL BE SOME LINGERING CLOUDS WITHIN A MIDLEVEL MOISTURE PLUME EXTENDING NEWD FROM THE SRN ROCKIES TO THE CENTRAL PLAINS. STILL...MODERATE BUOYANCY /MLCAPE AOA 2000 J PER KG/ IS EXPECTED IMMEDIATELY IN ADVANCE OF THE COLD FRONT...AND THE STRONGER STORMS ALONG THE FRONT WILL BE CAPABLE OF PRODUCING MARGINALLY SEVERE HAIL AND ISOLATED DAMAGING OUTFLOW GUSTS.

sections.title: SE ATLANTIC STATES THIS AFTERNOON
sections.text: A WEAKENING MIDLEVEL TROUGH IS DRIFTING OFF THE ATLANTIC COAST...WITH LINGERING WEAK NW FLOW OVER THE APPALACHIANS TO THE CAROLINAS. 12Z REGIONAL SOUNDINGS SHOW RATHER WARM MIDLEVEL TEMPERATURES AND MODEST LAPSE RATES...BUT MODERATE BUOYANCY IS STILL EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON WITH STRONG SURFACE HEATING OF A MOIST LOW-LEVEL AIR MASS. A FEW STRONG STORMS WILL BE POSSIBLE THIS AFTERNOON ALONG A WEAK SURFACE FRONT/TROUGH ACROSS SC/S GA...WHERE THERMODYNAMIC PROFILES WILL SUPPORT SOME RISK OF DOWNBURSTS. ..THOMPSON/PICCA.. 06/25/2016

outlooks.summary: SCATTERED SEVERE STORMS CAPABLE OF LARGE HAIL...DAMAGING WINDS...AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES ARE EXPECTED THIS AFTERNOON INTO EARLY TONIGHT ACROSS MUCH OF MINNESOTA AND WESTERN WISCONSIN. A MORE MARGINAL SEVERE STORM RISK WILL EXTEND SOUTHWESTWARD INTO THE CENTRAL PLAINS. ISOLATED STRONG STORMS ARE ALSO EXPECTED OVER PARTS OF THE SOUTHEAST.

sections.title: UPPER MS VALLEY AND WESTERN GREAT LAKES
sections.text: A STRONG UPPER LOW IS TRACKING EASTWARD ALONG THE MT/SASK BORDER. MID LEVEL HEIGHT FALLS AND LARGE SCALE LIFT AHEAD OF THIS FEATURE WILL BEGIN TO OVERSPREAD MN BY MID AFTERNOON...AIDING IN THE DEVELOPMENT OF THUNDERSTORMS ALONG A COLD FRONT. THE AIR MASS OVER MN IS RAPIDLY DESTABILIZING...WITH DEWPOINTS WELL INTO THE 70S AND FULL SUNSHINE YIELDING MLCAPE VALUES OF 3500 J/KG. INITIAL STORMS MAY BE SUPERCELLULAR DUE TO FAVORABLE DEEP LAYER AND LOW LEVEL SHEAR...POSING A RISK OF LARGE HAIL AND PERHAPS A TORNADO OR TWO. HOWEVER...IT APPEARS LIKELY THAT STORM OUTFLOWS WILL MERGE RELATIVELY QUICKLY...LEADING TO A PREDOMINANTLY LINEAR STORM MODE. STRENGTHENING LOW LEVEL WINDS AND STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL PROMOTE A RISK OF RATHER WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WINDS ACROSS EASTERN MN INTO WI AND UPPER MI.

sections.title: CENTRAL PLAINS
sections.text: THE SURFACE BOUNDARY WILL EXTEND SOUTHWESTWARD FROM MN INTO PARTS OF IA/NEB/KS BY LATE THIS AFTERNOON. THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO FORM WITHIN THE FRONTAL ZONE AND PERSIST THROUGH PARTS OF THE EVENING. VERTICAL SHEAR WILL BE WEAKER AND MID LEVEL TEMPERATURES WILL BE WARMER IN THIS REGION THAN FARTHER NORTH. HOWEVER...SUFFICIENT INSTABILITY AND STEEP LOW LEVEL LAPSE RATES INDICATE THE RISK OF STRONG DOWNDRAFTS IN THE MORE INTENSE CELLS.

sections.title: SOUTHEAST STATES
sections.text: WIDELY SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP LATER THIS AFTERNOON ALONG A WEAK BOUNDARY EXTENDING FROM SOUTHERN GA INTO SC. DESPITE WEAK VERTICAL SHEAR...HOT AND HUMID LOW LEVEL CONDITIONS WILL YIELD HIGH CAPE VALUES AND THE POTENTIAL FOR LOCALLY GUSTY/DAMAGING WINDS IN THE STRONGEST CORES. ..HART/COOK.. 06/25/2016

sections.text: NO CHANGES TO PREVIOUS FORECAST WARRANTED. ..DARROW.. 06/25/2016 .PREV DISCUSSION... /ISSUED 1122 AM CDT SAT JUN 25 2016/

outlooks.summary: A LINE OF OF STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS CAPABLE OF PRIMARILY DAMAGING WINDS WILL SPREAD ACROSS NORTHERN WISCONSIN AND WESTERN UPPER MICHIGAN THROUGH THIS EVENING...WITH THE OVERALL SEVERE-WEATHER THREAT DIMINISHING LATER TONIGHT. ISOLATED TO SCATTERED STRONG STORMS...SOME SEVERE...WILL REMAIN A THREAT ACROSS KANSAS INTO SOUTHEAST COLORADO AND NORTHEAST NEW MEXICO...MAINLY THIS EVENING...WHILE ADDITIONAL STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS MAY DEVELOP ACROSS IOWA TO NORTHEAST KANSAS THROUGH TONIGHT.

sections.title: UPPER GREAT LAKES
sections.text: MID-LEVEL SHORTWAVE TROUGH...CURRENTLY TRACKING EAST ALONG THE U.S./CANADA BORDER...WILL TRACK TO THE EAST-NORTHEAST THIS FORECAST PERIOD...REACHING NORTHWEST ONTARIO BY 12Z SUNDAY MORNING. A BAND OF 60-75-KT WESTERLY WINDS ATTENDANT TO THIS TROUGH WILL SPREAD ACROSS MN TO LAKE SUPERIOR AND NORTHERN ONTARIO. A SOUTHWESTERLY LOW-LEVEL JET STRENGTHENING TO 45-50 KT...AND EXTENDING INTO NORTHERN WI/UPPER MI TO LAKE SUPERIOR WILL MAINTAIN AN INFLUX OF MODERATELY STRONG INSTABILITY...AND ENHANCE DEEP LAYER SHEAR FOR SUSTAINED LINEAR STORM MODE. STRONG DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY SEVERE-WEATHER THREAT AS THE ONGOING LINEAR MCS ADVANCES ACROSS NORTHERN WI...UPPER MI AND LAKE SUPERIOR THIS EVENING TO THE EARLY OVERNIGHT PERIOD.

sections.title: NORTHEAST NM/SOUTHEAST CO THROUGH KS TO IA/NORTHERN MO
sections.text: A COLD FRONT WILL ADVANCE INTO THE UPPER GREAT LAKES REGION THROUGH TONIGHT...WITH THE TRAILING PORTION MOVING THROUGH IA AND INTO NORTHEAST KS BY 12Z...WHILE THE SOUTHERN EXTENT TENDS TO STALL ACROSS SOUTHWEST KS INTO NORTHEAST NM. LOCALLY STRONG WIND GUSTS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE WITH THE ONGOING STORMS EXTENDING FROM NORTH-CENTRAL KS TO NORTHEAST NM AND A FEW THAT REMAIN IN SOUTHEAST CO. HOWEVER...GRADUAL BOUNDARY-LAYER STABILIZATION THROUGH THIS EVENING SHOULD DIMINISH THIS THREAT. MEANWHILE...MODELS CONTINUE TO SUGGEST STORM COVERAGE COULD INCREASE ACROSS NORTHEAST KS THROUGH IA ALONG THE COLD FRONT...THOUGH THIS ACTIVITY HAS YET TO DEVELOP...OTHER THAN A FEW ISOLATED STORMS IN CENTRAL IA. RESIDUAL INSTABILITY AND POTENTIAL FORCING FOR ASCENT AS EMBEDDED MIDLEVEL IMPULSE IN THE NORTHEAST EXTENT OF MONSOONAL MOISTURE PLUME FROM THE SOUTHWEST STATES COULD SUPPORT STORM DEVELOPMENT. IF THIS OCCURS...THEN A FEW STRONGER WIND GUSTS AND/OR HAIL WOULD BE POSSIBLE. ..PETERS.. 06/26/2016

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THE SEVERE THREAT IS RAPIDLY INCREASING ACROSS PORTIONS OF MN EARLY THIS AFTERNOON. STORM ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP BY 20Z AND TRACK E/NE ACROSS MN INTO NRN WI. DAMAGING WINDS AND LARGE HAIL WILL BE THE PRIMARY CONCERN BUT A COUPLE OF TORNADOES ALSO ARE POSSIBLE.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: STRONG HEATING UNDER MOSTLY SUNNY SKIES HAS ALLOWED TEMPERATURES TO CLIMB INTO THE 80S TO NEAR 90 ACROSS MUCH OF SOUTHERN AND CENTRAL MN. COOLER TEMPERATURES WERE NOTED ACROSS NORTHEAST MN WHERE MORNING CONVECTION AND CLOUD COVER HAVE RESULTED IN SLOWER WARMING AND TEMPS IN THE 70S AS OF 1730Z. REGARDLESS...RAPID DESTABILIZATION IS OCCURRING WITH DEWPOINTS IN THE UPPER 60S AND LOWER 70S. MLCAPE AOA 2500 J/KG WAS NOTED IN 17Z MESOANALYSIS ACROSS MUCH OF THE MCD AREA. MEANWHILE...A COLD FRONT WAS DRAPED SOUTHWARD ACROSS WESTERN MN TO NEAR FSD IN SD AND ODX IN NEB...WHILE THE EFFECTIVE WARM FRONT EXTENDED SOUTHEASTWARD ACROSS NE MN INTO NORTHERN WI. THUNDERSTORMS ARE EXPECTED TO DEVELOP ALONG THE COLD FRONT WITHIN THE NEXT COUPLE OF HOURS A FORCING FOR ASCENT INCREASES WITH THE APPROACH OF THE UPPER SHORTWAVE AND ENVIRONMENT QUICKLY BECOMES UNCAPPED. AREA VWP/S SHOW MODEST VERTICALLY VEERED LOW LEVEL HODOGRAPHS ACROSS SRN/CNTRL MN WITH GREATER LOW LEVEL CURVATURE NEAR THE WARM FRONT/TRIPLE POINT WHERE LOW LEVEL WINDS ARE MORE SELY. SUPERCELLS WILL INITIALLY BE POSSIBLE AND MAY POSE A THREAT FOR ALL HAZARDS INCLUDING DAMAGING WINDS...LARGE HAIL AND A COUPLE OF TORNADOES. STRONGER DEEP LAYER SHEAR IS EXPECTED TO TRAIL THE SYNOPTIC COLD FRONT LEADING TO FAIRLY RAPID UPSCALE GROWTH INTO LINEAR BOWING SEGMENTS. WHILE LARGE HAIL AND A TORNADO OR TWO MAY STILL BE POSSIBLE AFTER UPSCALE GROWTH COMMENCES...DAMAGING WIND IS EXPECTED TO BE THE PRIMARY CONCERN. A WATCH WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED BY 20Z.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SEVERE STORMS ARE EXPECTED THROUGH THE EVENING HOURS ACROSS ERN NEB AND WRN IA. DAMAGING WINDS AND HAIL ARE THE PRIMARY CONCERN AND A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED THIS AFTERNOON.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORMS HAVE BEGUN TO DEVELOP ALONG THE COLD FRONT IN FAR SE SD AND NE NEB. MESOANALYSIS AND FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST SOME MIDLEVEL INHIBITION IS PRESENT...BUT SHOULD ERODE WITH CONTINUED HEATING AND INCREASED FORCING. HOWEVER AREAS OF CLOUDINESS DOWNSTREAM FROM THE COLD FRONT MAKE TIMING OF SEVERE STORM DEVELOPMENT ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR A BIT MORE UNCERTAIN. DESPITE THIS...DEWPOINTS CURRENTLY IN THE UPPER 60S TO LOW 70S BENEATH STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES HAS LED TO MODERATE INSTABILITY ACROSS THE WARM SECTOR. DEEP LAYER EFFECTIVE SHEAR IS ON THE LOWER SIDE FOR WELL-ORGANIZED STORMS...BUT SHOULD BE SUFFICIENT FOR A MIX OF SEMI-DISCRETE CELLS AND BOWING LINE SEGMENTS. DCAPE VALUES GREATER THAN 1200 J/KG WERE NOTED IN 18Z MESOANALYSIS AND WILL AID IN DAMAGING WIND THREAT THROUGH THE EVENING. ADDITIONALLY...STEEP MIDLEVEL LAPSE RATES AND LARGE CAPE VALUES WILL SUPPORT SEVERE HAIL...THOUGH STORM MODE MAY LIMIT SIG HAIL POTENTIAL. A SEVERE THUNDERSTORM WATCH WILL LIKELY BE NEEDED THIS AFTERNOON.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: SOME ISOLATED HAIL AND/OR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS POSSIBLE DURING THE NEXT HOUR OR TWO. A GREATER SVR THREAT IS POSSIBLE LATER THIS EVENING.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: TSTMS HAVE DEVELOPED QUICKLY WITHIN THE WAA REGIME AHEAD OF THE APPROACHING SHORTWAVE TROUGH AND ASSOCIATED COLD FRONT /FARTHER W ACROSS MN/. SURFACE ANALYSIS ACROSS THE REGION REVEALS AN OUTFLOW BOUNDARY VERY NEAR THE WI/MI BORDER. RECENT MESOANALYSIS AND FORECAST SOUNDINGS SUGGEST MORE MLCINH EXISTS ALONG AND N OF THIS BOUNDARY /LARGELY AS A RESULT OF WARM MID-LEVEL TEMPERATURES AND SLIGHTLY COOLER SURFACE TEMPERATURES/ THAN ACROSS AREAS FARTHER S AND W WHERE THE TSTMS INITIATED. AS A RESULT...THE GENERAL EXPECTATION WITH THIS ACTIVITY IS FOR PERSISTENCE AND PERHAPS ADDITIONAL DEVELOPMENT ACROSS NE WI WITH THESE TSTMS GRADUALLY DIMINISHING AS THEY CONTINUE NEWD INTO A MORE HOSTILE AIRMASS. SOME BRIEF INTENSIFICATION IS POSSIBLE AS THE TSTMS INTERACT WITH THE REMNANT OUTFLOW BOUNDARY. MODERATE INSTABILITY /MLCAPE FROM 1500 TO 2000 J PER KG/ AMIDST INCREASING MID-LEVEL FLOW AND STRENGTHENING VERTICAL SHEAR /EFFECTIVE BULK SHEAR CURRENTLY NEAR 30-35 KT/ WILL SUPPORT A FEW STRONG STORMS CAPABLE OF ISOLATED HAIL AND/OR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS. A GREATER SVR THREAT MAY BE REALIZED LATER THIS EVENING AS THE ACTIVITY ACROSS MN ALONG THE COLD FRONT CONTINUE EWD. THIS POTENTIAL THREAT WOULD BE ADDRESSED IN A LATER DISCUSSION.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: ISOLATED SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS PRODUCING DAMAGING DOWNBURST WINDS WILL REMAIN POSSIBLE THROUGH EARLY EVENING. A WATCH IS NOT ANTICIPATED.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: ISOLATED TO WIDELY SCATTERED THUNDERSTORMS HAVE DEVELOPED ALONG A COLD FRONT THAT EXTENDS FROM NORTH-CENTRAL KS SOUTHWEST INTO SOUTHEAST COLORADO...AND ALONG A SURFACE TROUGH OF LOW PRESSURE FROM SOUTHEAST CO INTO NORTHEAST NEW MEXICO. STRONG DIURNAL HEATING HAS RESULTED IN MLCAPE OF 1000 TO 2000 J/KG...HOWEVER GENERALLY WEAK LOW-MID LEVEL FLOW ALOFT/DEEP-LAYER SHEAR BELOW 25 KTS WILL LIMIT STORM ORGANIZATION. SURFACE DEW POINTS RANGE FROM THE LOWER-MID 50S ACROSS THE CO/NM PORTION OF THE DISCUSSION AREA TO THE LOWER 60S OVER WESTERN KS. WITH STEEP LOW-LEVEL LAPSE RATES AND LOW RH VALUES IN THE SUB-CLOUD LAYER...THE STRONGER STORMS WILL HAVE THE POTENTIAL FOR DAMAGING GUSTS THROUGH EARLY EVENING. THE OVERALL THREAT IS EXPECTED TO REMAIN ISOLATED AND A WATCH IS NOT EXPECTED.

mesoscale_discussions.summary: DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND SOME ISOLATED HAIL ARE POSSIBLE AS THE CLUSTER OF STORMS FROM E OF DLH SWWD TO AROUND MIC CONTINUE EWD. CURRENT MOTION TAKES THESE STORMS THROUGH THE REMAINDER OF TOR WATCH 298 AND TO THE ERN EDGE OF WW 299 AROUND 00Z AND A DOWNSTREAM WATCH MAY BE NEEDED ACROSS PORTIONS OF UPPER MI AND N-CNTRL/NE WI.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: RECENT RADAR IMAGERY OF THE CLUSTER OF TSTMS MOVING THROUGH THE FAR NRN MN/WI BORDER HAS SHOWN AN EWD SURGE IN REFLECTIVITY COINCIDENT WITH A BIT MORE FORWARD PROPAGATION AND LINEAR ORGANIZATION OF THE CLUSTER. SURFACE ANALYSIS PLACES THE COMPOSITE OUTFLOW/LAKE BREEZE/WARM FRONT FROM DLH EWD/ESEWD ALONG THE WI/MI BORDER. CURRENT EXPECTATION IS FOR THE CLUSTER OF TSTMS TO CONTINUE TO MOVE ESEWD ALONG /OR VERY NEAR/ THE SURFACE BOUNDARY WITH FURTHER LINEAR ORGANIZATION POSSIBLE. THE STRONGER MID-LEVEL FLOW IS STILL FARTHER W...SUGGESTING WIDESPREAD DAMAGING WIND GUSTS ARE UNLIKELY. HOWEVER...OCCASIONAL STRONG GUSTS ASSOCIATED WITH FORWARD-PROPAGATING SEGMENTS AND/OR LOCALIZED DOWNBURSTS ARE PROBABLE FOR THE NEXT SEVERAL HOURS. STEEP MID-LEVEL LAPSE RATES WILL ALSO SUPPORT SOME HAIL WITH THE STRONGEST UPDRAFTS. CURRENT STORM MOTION...APPROXIMATELY 270/33 KT...TAKES THE CLUSTER TO THE EDGE OF THE CURRENT WATCH AROUND 00Z. TRENDS WILL BE MONITORED CLOSELY AND DOWNSTREAM WATCH MAY BE NEEDED TO COVER THE IMPENDING SVR THREAT. ..MOSIER.. 06/25/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.summary: THREAT FOR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS AND ISOLATED HAIL CONTINUES ACROSS NRN WI AND WRN UPPER MI.
mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CONVECTIVE LINE CONTINUES TO MOVE EWD ACROSS NRN WI AND INTO WRN UPPER MI WITH ESTIMATED STORM MOTION OF 270/38 KT. AIRMASS AHEAD OF THE BOWING PORTION OF THE LINE -- ROUGHLY ACROSS IRON AND PRICE COUNTIES IN FAR NRN WI AT 0105Z -- REMAINS UNSTABLE WITH RECENT MESOANALYSIS ESTIMATING MLCAPE NEAR 1500-2000 J PER KG. RECENT VAD DATA FROM ARX HAS SHOWN A MODEST INCREASE IN WLY WIND SPEEDS IN THE 1-2 KM LAYER AND MQT VAD SHOWS SWLY WINDS HAVE INCREASED TO 50-55 KT AROUND 1 KM. THIS INCREASE IN CROSS-BOUNDARY WINDS COMBINED WITH DOWNSTREAM INSTABILITY WILL LIKELY PROMOTE THE PERSISTENCE...AND PERHAPS STRENGTHENING...OF THE LINE. AS SUCH...THE THREAT FOR DAMAGING WIND GUSTS CONTINUES. SOME HAIL IS ALSO POSSIBLE...PARTICULARLY WITH ANY UPDRAFT STRENGTHENING RESULTING FROM CELL MERGERS. ..MOSIER.. 06/26/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...

mesoscale_discussions.discussion: THUNDERSTORMS HAVE RECENTLY DEVELOPED ALONG A COLD FRONT THAT EXTENDS FROM NORTH-CENTRAL IOWA SOUTHWEST ACROSS SOUTHEAST NEBRASKA. LATEST MESOANALYSIS REVEALS A MODERATE-STRONGLY UNSTABLE ENVIRONMENT...AND 40 KT MID-LEVEL FLOW WILL CONTRIBUTE TO SUFFICIENT DEEP-LAYER SHEAR /30-35 KT/ FOR STORM ORGANIZATION. THE DISCUSSION AREA LIES ON THE SOUTHERN FRINGE OF LARGE-SCALE ASCENT ASSOCIATED WITH AN UPPER-LEVEL LOW OVER SOUTHERN MANITOBA...AND THIS COMBINED WITH FRONTAL CONVERGENCE SHOULD RESULT IN SOME INCREASE IN STORM COVERAGE DURING THE REMAINDER OF THE EVENING DESPITE THE ONSET OF NOCTURNAL COOLING. THE STRONGER STORMS WILL BE CAPABLE OF SEVERE HAIL AND WIND GUSTS FOR A FEW HOURS...BUT THE OVERALL RISK SHOULD REMAIN ISOLATED AND A WATCH IS NOT EXPECTED.

mesoscale_discussions.discussion: CONVECTIVE LINE ACROSS NRN WI AND WRN UPPER MI HAS BECOME ORIENTED MORE SW TO NE OVER THE PAST HOUR AS THE NRN PORTION OF THE LINE ENCOUNTERED THE MORE STABLE AIRMASS ACROSS UPPER MI. REORIENTATION OF THE LINE HAS RESULTED IN A MORE PERPENDICULAR ORIENTATION TO THE LOW-LEVEL FLOW WITH A RESULTING DECREASE IN FORWARD PROPAGATION SPEED. A FEW DAMAGING WIND GUSTS ARE STILL POSSIBLE BUT THE OVERALL SVR THREAT WILL CONTINUE TO DIMINISH. PRIMARY THREAT NOW APPEARS TO BE HEAVY RAINFALL. WW 299 WILL BE ALLOWED TO EXPIRE AT 04Z AS THE THREAT IS OVER ACROSS THE MAJORITY OF THE REMAINING WATCH AREA. THE ONLY EXCEPTION IS OVER CHIPPEWA AND EAU CLAIRE COUNTIES WERE A FEW TSTMS REMAINS. STORMS IN THESE COUNTIES ARE NOT EXPECTED TO REACH SVR THRESHOLDS AND WILL LIKELY BE NEAR THE ERN EDGES OR THROUGH THE COUNTIES BY 04Z. ..MOSIER.. 06/26/2016 ...PLEASE SEE WWW.SPC.NOAA.GOV FOR GRAPHIC PRODUCT...
